groupings.title: 1. Design — Entry Point
groupings.description: Mandatory starting point. Turns a vague request into a structured engineering project by enforcing the 7-category Brief before any artifact is built.

groupings.title: 2. Construction — Build the Artifacts
groupings.description: Produce the three independent artifacts: the live ISO (archiso), the persistent .img appliance (EFI+SYS+DATA), and the offline signed pacman repository embedded in the ISO.

groupings.title: 3. Payloads & Desktop — Extend the System
groupings.description: Declare and materialize app payloads from their own repositories (never vendorized), and choose the graphical layer from L0 (console-only) to L6 (GNOME/KDE).

groupings.title: 4. Validation — Gates Before Real Hardware
groupings.description: Two mandatory gates: QEMU validation (15 ISO checks, 13 .img checks) and safe physical hardware writes. No artifact reaches a real disk without passing both.

groupings.title: 5. Knowledge Base — Memory of Real Failures
groupings.description: A living, dated catalog of real errors found while building Arch ISOs and appliances (community 404, DisableDownloadTimeout, error -71, SDDM hangs, etc.). Consulted before every build.
